The Jade Viceroy's couriers whisper that [From.GetSubjectPronoun] delights in [From.Offmap.GetLike] but cannot abide [From.Offmap.GetDislike].

The House of [FromFrom.GetOnlyDynastyName] has lost the favour of Heaven, and the House of [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] has taken the Dragon Throne in its place. The new [From.GetEmperorEmpress], [From.GetDynName], keeps to the [From.Offmap.GetPolicy] Policy of the fallen house, for now. [FromFrom.GetEmperorEmpress] [FromFrom.GetDynName], who held to the [From.Offmap.GetPrevPolicy] Policy, has gone to join the ancestors, and [From.GetDynName] now sits upon the Dragon Throne in Wei-Jin. The new [From.GetEmperorEmpress] has already broken with [From.GetPossPronoun] predecessor and proclaimed an [From.Offmap.GetPolicy] Cathay. It is said that [From.GetSubjectPronoun] delights in [From.Offmap.GetLike] but cannot abide [From.Offmap.GetDislike].

The House of [FromFrom.GetOnlyDynastyName] has lost the favour of Heaven, and the House of [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] has taken the Dragon Throne in its place. The new [From.GetEmperorEmpress], [From.GetDynName], has swept aside the [From.Offmap.GetPrevPolicy] Policy of the fallen house and proclaimed an [From.Offmap.GetPolicy] Cathay. It is said that [From.GetSubjectPronoun] delights in [From.Offmap.GetLike] but cannot abide [From.Offmap.GetDislike].
May the caravans keep coming.
Then the gates of the Great Bastion stay shut.
The Dragon stirs. We had best be ready.
Our pact was with the old house. It binds us no longer.

Cathay has put aside its [FromFrom.GetPrevPolicy] ways. The gates of the Great Bastion stand open again, and the jade, silk and black powder of the east flow west to any lord with gold to pay for them.

Cathay has gone from [FromFrom.GetPrevPolicy] to Isolationist. The [FromFrom.Ruler.GetSonDaughterCap] of Heaven, [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName], has turned [FromFrom.Ruler.GetPossPronoun] back on the barbarian lands beyond the Great Bastion in order to [GetCathayIsolationPastime]. The caravans east will find the gates barred.

[FromFrom.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName] of Cathay has turned [FromFrom.Ruler.GetPossPronoun] gaze west. Jade armies march along the roads beyond the Great Bastion, and lords who have not earned the favour of the Celestial Court would do well to fear this new Expansionist Policy.\n\nThe Dragon is awake.
Barbarians, are we? So be it.
[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. Order returns to the provinces of Grand Cathay, and the caravans set out west once more.

[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. Peasant risings have broken out in [GetRandomCathayanRegion], where mobs led by [GetRandomCathayanFaction] burn the granaries of the mandarins. Trade on the roads east has fallen by a quarter, and Cathay cannot defend its Tributaries.

[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. The rains have failed and the rice paddies of Cathay lie cracked and dry. A Great Famine stalks the land, the caravans have all but stopped, and Cathay cannot help its Tributaries.

[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. A pestilence has broken out in [GetRandomCathayanRegion], and the dead are piled in the streets faster than the priests can burn them. Some blame the ratmen, others the Plague God of the north. No merchant dares take the roads east, and the sickness may yet come west along them. Cathay cannot help its Tributaries.

[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. A great Hobgoblin horde has slipped past the watchtowers of the Great Bastion and pours into the northern provinces, burning and looting as it comes. [FromFrom.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName] musters [FromFrom.Ruler.GetPossPronoun] armies in [GetRandomCathayanRegion], but the war may be long.\n\nWhile it lasts, the trade east is halved and Cathay cannot help its Tributaries.

[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. The Man-chu, the fiercest of the Hung tribes, have united under a Chaos-sworn Khagan and ride into the north-east of Cathay with numberless horsemen. [FromFrom.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName] gathers [FromFrom.Ruler.GetPossPronoun] armies in [GetRandomCathayanRegion], but many towns are already in flames.\n\nWhile it lasts, the trade east is halved and Cathay cannot help its Tributaries.

[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. Civil war rocks Cathay: a rebel governor has won over the generals of [GetRandomCathayanRegion] and marches on Wei-Jin. Trade on the roads east is halved, and Tributaries may seize the chance to break free, for Cathay cannot defend them.

[FromFrom.GetCathayPreviousStatusEnd]. Harmony and plenty bloom across Cathay under the wise rule of [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName]. New silks, porcelain and wonders of the alchemists flow west along roads safer than any living man remembers, and the wealth of the trade east has doubled!

With Cathay already suffering from the [offmap_cathay.GetPrevStatus], a great Hobgoblin horde has seized its chance and crossed the Great Bastion into the north. Will the wolf riders of the steppe break the Dragon's back?

At the height of a golden age, a great Hobgoblin horde has hurled itself against the Great Bastion, meaning to take the whole empire. But the Dragon is mighty, and the wolf riders are in for a titanic struggle.
Let them bleed each other.

After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the armies of Cathay have won a decisive victory near [GetRandomCathayanRegion]. The Hobgoblin Khagan is slain, his wolf riders cut down to the last, and his head hangs from the gate of the Great Bastion.
The Dragon's teeth are sharp still.

After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the Hobgoblins stand triumphant. The last battle was fought near [GetRandomCathayanRegion], and now the Hobgoblin Khagan sits upon the Dragon Throne as [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetDynName], founder of a new house! Cathay will know Unrest for many years to come.

After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the Hobgoblin hordes have broken the western defences and put the provinces near [GetRandomCathayanRegion] to the torch. Yet the Dragon Throne does not fall. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetDynName], the immortal Dragon Emperor, has paid the Khagan a fortune in jade and silk to take his hordes home. Cathay is shaken, and unrest is likely to follow.
Who would have thought it?

With Cathay already suffering from the [offmap_cathay.GetPrevStatus], a new misfortune has struck: the Man-chu have united under a Chaos-sworn Khagan and their horsemen pour into the north-east. This is no raid to test the defences of the Great Bastion.

At the height of a golden age, a great Man-chu horde has crossed into the north-east of Cathay, meaning to take the whole empire. But the riches of the Dragon's land are guarded by a million well-armed soldiers, and the Hung riders are in for a titanic struggle.

After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the armies of Cathay have won a decisive victory near [GetRandomCathayanRegion]. The Man-chu Khagan is slain, his chosen riders cut down to the last, and the Hung flee north to their frozen steppe.
The Dragon's teeth are sharp still.

After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the Man-chu stand triumphant. The last battle was fought near [GetRandomCathayanRegion], and now their Khagan sits upon the Dragon Throne as [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetDynName], founder of a new house! Shrines to the Dark Gods rise in Wei-Jin, and Cathay will know Unrest for many years to come.

After years of war and battles of hundreds of thousands, the Man-chu have broken through and plundered the provinces near [GetRandomCathayanRegion]. Yet the Dragon Throne does not fall. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetDynName], the immortal Dragon Emperor, has driven the Khagan back beyond the Great Bastion at a terrible price. Cathay is shaken, and unrest is likely to follow.
Even the Dragon can be wounded.

The long Unrest in Cathay has flared into open Civil War! Many say that [FromFrom.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName] is weak and has lost the Mandate of Heaven. While [FromFrom.Ruler.GetSubjectPronoun] shelters in [GetRandomCathayanRegion], rebel armies storm loyal strongholds. The rebels have no single leader yet and fight each other as often as the throne. Trade east is halved, and Tributaries may seize the chance to break free.
A house divided...

The Cathayan Civil War has ended. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetDynName] has crushed the main rebel army in [GetRandomCathayanRegion], ending long years of war between loyalists, rabble-rousing monks, pretenders and an over-ambitious governor. Order returns to Cathay and the roads east are safe again.
Interesting.

After long years of war and shifting alliances, the Cathayan Civil War is over. A warrior monk of [GetRandomCathayanRegion] has beaten the loyalists and every rival faction, and now rules as [FromFrom.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName]. A child of the common folk, the new [FromFrom.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] has purged the corrupt mandarins of the old court. Order returns to Cathay and the roads east are safe again.

After long years of war and shifting alliances, the Cathayan Civil War is over. The foreign house has fallen, and Cathay is ruled once more by one of its own: [FromFrom.Ruler.GetDynName], once governor of [GetRandomCathayanRegion], has beaten the loyalists and every rival faction to take the Dragon Throne. Order returns to Cathay and the roads east are safe again.

After long years of war and shifting alliances, the Cathayan Civil War is over. The old court has fallen, and [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetEmperorEmpress] [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetDynName], a pretender of the [offmap_cathay.Ruler.Dynasty.GetName], now sits upon the Dragon Throne. Order returns to Cathay and the roads east are safe again.

The End Times have reached the east. Out of the Northern Wastes a horde beyond counting has fallen on the Great Bastion, the wall that has guarded Cathay since the first Dragon Emperor. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has called every army in the empire north to hold it.

Ogre tribes have come down out of the Mountains of Mourning and are eating their way through the western provinces of Cathay. The frontier garrisons are fighting them valley by valley, and the caravans on the Silk Road are being plundered.

Strange news from Cathay: wells turning foul, officials dying in their beds, whole storehouses of jade vanishing overnight. The Cathayans say ratmen are tunnelling beneath their cities, and [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetTitledFirstName] has sent soldiers down into the dark after them.

The Great Bastion has held. After years of slaughter on the wall, the hordes of the north have broken and fled back into the Wastes, leaving their dead piled at its foot. Cathay has paid dearly for the victory and the empire is restless, but the Dragon Throne still stands.

The unthinkable has happened. The Great Bastion has fallen and the hordes of the north have stormed the capital. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetBestName], a warlord of the Ruinous Powers, now sits on the Dragon Throne. Of the Dragon Emperor nothing is known, except that his body was not found.

The Dragon Emperor has returned. [offmap_cathay.Ruler.GetBestName] came down on the capital in his true form, and the Chaos warlord who had taken his throne was burnt where he stood. The servants of the Ruinous Powers are being hunted out of Cathay province by province.

The northern hordes have broken through the Great Bastion and put the northern provinces of Cathay to the torch before they were driven out. Fields lie burnt and granaries empty, and famine is spreading through the empire.
The Ogres have finally gone home, but not before eating the western granaries of Cathay bare. Famine is spreading through the provinces they passed through.

Rather than fight the Ogres valley by valley, the Dragon Throne has paid them to go home, and paid well. The tribes have gone back to the Mountains of Mourning laden with silver, and the Ogre Kingdoms of the west are spending it already.
The Ogre tribes have been driven back into the Mountains of Mourning. The western garrisons have rebuilt their forts, and the caravans are moving again.
Before they were driven out, the ratmen poisoned the wells of Cathay. A terrible plague is now spreading through its cities.
The war beneath Cathay is over. The tunnels under its cities have been flooded and sealed, and the ratmen burnt out of their warrens. The empire is calm again.
The ratmen have gone back underground, and a great deal of Cathay's jade and warpstone has gone with them. The Under-Empire is richer for it, and the Cathayan court is looking for someone to blame.
Troubling news.
